MARKUP DEVIATION REPORT - DataForge SPA (Seller markup of May 2, 2025 vs. Buyer draft of April 18, 2025)
To: J. Hartwell; for escalation to C. Westbrook. Privileged.

1. BOTTOM LINE
The markup trips at least 12 playbook walk-away/approval triggers and changes all three elements of the integrated indemnity package (holdback, cap, basket). Playbook Sec. 9.3 and Sec. 11 therefore require escalation to Westbrook and Hartwell before any response, and a written summary at least 24 hours before the proposed call (week of May 5). The cover letter understates the markup. Roughly a dozen material changes are not mentioned in it, several are untracked, and the Sellers' HSR/338 premises need checking. Do not respond on the cover-letter list alone.

2. REDLINE INTEGRITY (threshold issue)
- The markup is not a clean redline of our draft. It has 87 tracked insertions/deletions, but it also renumbers the agreement (conditions moved from Art. VIII to VI; indemnity from IX to VIII), rewrites provisions without tracking, and adds untracked bracketed text with "NV Comment" notes (e.g., Sec. 2.8 earnout, Sec. 9.15 reverse fee, Sec. 10.12 arbitration). The cover letter's article references do not match the document. Request a true machine redline against the April 18 draft and run our own full comparison before signing anything.
- NV comment to Sec. 2.2 says the consideration restructuring reflects "the commercial agreement reached during our April 28 call." Nothing in our file records any such agreement (deal memo: no earnout expected). Confirm with Zhou/Hartwell; reject the characterization in writing.

3. DEVIATIONS (Original -> Markup | Playbook | Assessment/Response)
Tracked and disclosed in cover letter:
(a) Closing cash $112.0M -> $102.0M; new $10.0M all-or-nothing earnout on FY2026 Net Revenue >= $72.0M (Secs. 2.2, 2.8). Playbook: earnouts disfavored; Westbrook approval required; guardrails: <= 5% of equity ($6.375M), measured <= 12 months post-closing, no efforts covenant, no separate books, objective GAAP metric, Buyer sole discretion. Markup: $10M = 7.8%; FY2026 ends about 17.5 months after a July 15, 2025 closing (payment later); commercially reasonable efforts (2.8(d)); separate books through 12/31/2027 (2.8(e)); anti-diversion with cross-sell revenue deemed Company revenue (2.8(f)). Base case FY2026 revenue is $69.5M, $2.5M below threshold (workbook; upside $73.1M). Operating covenants are a stated walk-away. NOT DISCLOSED: 2.8(g) accelerates the full $10M on any merger/consolidation involving Buyer or the Company or a >50% change of control. Our own Phase 3 integration (unified codebase, months 13-18) and any sponsor exit would trigger it. Response: reject; if Westbrook authorizes, cap at $6.375M, 12-month test, no covenants/separate books/acceleration, sole discretion language.
(b) Holdback/escrow ($15.5M, 18 months, setoff) -> "Deferred Consideration" paid $7.75M at 12 and 24 months, unconditional, no setoff, 8% default interest (2.7); escrow agreement, agent and Sec. 8.2(h) "holdback first" deleted. Playbook Must-Have; walk-away is elimination of holdback or removal of setoff. Cover letter says only "timing". It is a conversion of security into a debt owed to Sellers. Response: reject; fallback only partial release (50% at 12 months) if no pending claims, escrow and setoff intact.
(c) NWC collar $200K -> $500K (2.5(d), Sched. 2.5). 5.95% of the $8.4M target vs. 3% max ($252K). Workbook shows $300K added exposure. Adjustment beyond the collar remains full (first-dollar). Response: counter $200K; settle no higher than $252K.
(d) Sec. 338(h)(10) prohibition added to tax covenant (7.8(f)) with Seller acknowledgment of "ordinary income." Playbook: strong preference; prohibition needs deal partner approval; value $8-12M PV (50-75 bps IRR). See Sec. 4 below on availability. Response: hold; trade only for value.
(e) Customer consents (Northland $8.9M, Greystone $7.1M, Summit $6.4M; $22.4M ARR, 34.9%) removed as condition and closing deliverable; replaced by post-closing "reasonable best efforts" covenant (7.11) that expires 90 days after closing, with Sellers expressly not liable for failure. Orion consent remains. Playbook Strong Preference, Priority 1 in Sec. 9.3. Fallback: Northland remains a condition; Greystone/Summit become covenants with an uncapped specific indemnity outside basket. Workbook: 0 of 12 change-of-control consents obtained (12 contracts = $35.6M ARR, 55.5%); Summit's contract expires 8/31/2025, Northland 3/14/2026, Greystone 5/31/2026 so renewals are also at risk.
(f) Reverse termination fee $6,375,000 (5%), Sec. 9.15, payable on Seller termination (outside date or Buyer breach) where the "primary reason" for non-closing is Buyer's financing. Playbook: none; max 3% ($3.825M); counter 2% ($2.55M); conditions: all Seller conditions satisfied, no Seller breach, sole remedy including no specific performance. Markup lacks those conditions and keeps Fraud/Willful Breach claims outside the fee, so exposure may exceed 5%. Cover letter says fee also covers "breach by Buyer"; text covers financing failure only. Note it also contradicts the comment that Buyer's obligations are not financing-conditioned.
(g) Non-compete 3 years/US-wide -> 18 months/IL, CA, NY, TX, FL only (7.10, Ex. C). Playbook: minimum 2 years nationwide for founders receiving > $20M (Anand ~$66.3M; Deshmukh ~$35.7M); never concede duration and scope together. Both are conceded: walk-away. Response: accept 2 years nationwide at most. See enforceability note below.
(h) Dispute resolution: Delaware Chancery exclusive jurisdiction replaced by AAA arbitration in Chicago, three arbitrators, loser-pays fees, no punitive damages, Cook County courts for interim relief (10.12); jury waiver deleted. Playbook walk-away: Chicago arbitration without expanded discovery; fallback Wilmington seat, Chancery-equivalent discovery, M&A-experienced panel.
(i) Outside date 9/30/2025 -> 8/31/2025 (9.1(b)). Playbook floor 9/15/2025. See HSR issue.
(j) Indemnity: general cap 10% ($12.75M) -> 7% ($8.925M); basket 0.75% ($956,250) tipping -> 1.25% ($1,593,750) true deductible (8.4); survival 18 -> 12 months (8.1). Playbook: cap floor 8.5% ($10.8375M); basket max 1.0% ($1.275M) if tipping, 0.50% ($637,500) if deductible; survival floor 15 months (below is walk-away). Combined with (b), all three package elements move; escalation mandatory. The cover letter calls this "market-conforming" without numbers.

NOT in cover letter (several untracked):
(k) Governing law Delaware -> Illinois (10.11). Playbook Must-Have; non-Delaware law is a walk-away. Not mentioned in cover letter.
(l) Knowledge: "after reasonable inquiry" deleted; group cut to Anand and Deshmukh (Huang and Patel removed in Sched. 1.1(a)). Playbook Must-Have/walk-away on both.
(m) Data privacy rep 4.20(c) now knowledge- and "material liability"-qualified; Schedule 4.20(c) deleted, removing disclosure of the Sept. 2023 incident (14,000 PII records, no regulator notice). Playbook Must-Have: unqualified rep and full disclosure. Schedule 8.2 (specified indemnities) now reads "None": no special indemnity for the IRS FY2022 audit ($1.8M), Sept. 2023 incident, or the four contractors lacking IP assignments, each of which the playbook requires uncapped.
(n) Exclusivity covenant (our Sec. 5.3) is gone, though the cover letter cites Sellers' "agreeing to exclusivity" to justify the reverse fee. Notification-of-changes covenant also gone.
(o) Seller liability changed from joint and several for founders to several by Pro Rata Share only (8.2); the 20% "Other Holders" (angels/option holders) are no longer named parties, yet are in the Shares and Pro Rata Share definitions. Buyer cannot deliver 100% of the Shares or recover 20% of any loss. Walk-away-level structural issue.
(p) Fraud: new narrow common-law definition (scienter; no recklessness) and 8.4(e) makes the Fundamental Rep Cap ($127.5M) the cap on Fraud/Willful Breach claims; our draft left fraud and pre-closing taxes outside all caps. Playbook Must-Have: uncapped fraud. Pre-closing tax exclusion from caps also dropped; covenant indemnity limited to pre-closing covenants. Cite for the principle that sellers cannot insulate themselves from deliberate fraud in the contract's own reps: ABRY Partners V, L.P. v. F&W Acquisition LLC, 891 A.2d 1032 (Del. Ch. 2006) (persuasive/Delaware; not verified live).
(q) Bring-down: "de minimis" exception added to Fundamental Representations; Non-Competition Agreement and no-proceedings closing conditions dropped; consent flexibility ("conditioned") added to interim-operating-covenant approvals; IRS audit control moved to Sellers' Representative.
(r) Jury trial waiver and Exhibit D deleted (follow-on to (b),(h)).

4. FACTUAL AND LEGAL ISSUES BEHIND THE POSITIONS
HSR (our error, not Sellers'). Our draft (Sec. 8.1(b); memo Sec. I, VII.G; playbook Sec. 5.1) says no HSR filing because the deal is below a $119.5M threshold. That was the 2024 figure. The 2025 size-of-transaction threshold, effective Feb. 21, 2025, is $126.4M (15 U.S.C. 18a; FTC annual adjustment notice, not independently verified). Equity value is $127.5M; a deferred/earnout structure does not lower the acquisition price because contingent consideration is valued and counted. The size-of-person test applies between $126.4M and $505.8M: Pinnacle (~$385M revenue) and DataForge ($64.2M) likely satisfy it. A filing is therefore probably required, with a 30-day waiting period and new, longer HSR form (effective Feb. 10, 2025). The Meridian workbook itself flags this. Consequences: the 8/31 outside date is unrealistic for a May 16 signing; the 6.1(a) condition is wrongly drafted as a no-filing representation; gun-jumping rules constrain interim covenants. The playbook's own text instructs confirmation with Zhou. Fix the draft proactively; this strengthens the Sept. 15-30 outside-date position without reliance on Seller concessions. Thresholds must be re-checked as of filing.
338(h)(10). Availability is doubtful. The election requires a target that is an S corporation or a member of a selling consolidated/affiliated group (Treas. Reg. 1.338(h)(10)-1) and joint election by sellers. DataForge has angel investors, a $3.0M income tax provision (~24% rate) and NOLs, indicating a C corporation owned by individuals. If so, the election is unavailable, the $8-12M benefit in the memo is unsupported, and the prohibition costs Buyer nothing (but should still be traded, not given). Confirm tax status with tax advisors before positioning. Sellers' statement of "ordinary income" is also unreliable.
Non-compete enforceability. The cover letter invokes Illinois law (820 ILCS 90). The Illinois Freedom to Work Act, as I recall it, excludes covenants ancillary to the sale of a business ownership interest, and California Bus. & Prof. Code 16601 expressly permits sale-of-business covenants within the area where the business was carried on. Both points need verification; they undercut the stated enforceability rationale for a five-state limit. Conversely, the playbook's statement that Delaware regularly enforces nationwide covenants is overconfident: Delaware has refused to enforce or blue-pencil overbroad sale-of-business covenants (Kodiak Building Partners v. Adams (Del. Ch. 2022); Intertek Testing Services NA v. Eastman (Del. Ch. 2023); verify). Support nationwide scope with the customer list (50-state footprint) and tailor "connected in any manner" and the Buyer-affiliate non-solicit language to the Company's business.
Cash double count (our draft). NWC includes $5.0M cash, and Net Debt also credits $5.0M closing cash. Confirm with Meridian that cash is not counted twice in the purchase price and NWC adjustment. Also Q4 2024 NWC is shown as $9.4M against $8.4M on the year-end balance sheet; the target average depends on it.
Lender naming. Cover letter says "Great Lakes Fidelity Bank"; all internal documents say Great Lakes Hartleigh Bank. Confirm legal name before any commitment-letter references.

5. DOCUMENT CONSISTENCY NOTES
Deal memo FY2025/FY2027 revenue ($67.4M/$74.8M) differs from workbook ($66.8M/$75.2M); FY2026 base case $69.5M matches. FY2024 "Adjusted EBITDA" ($13.8M) is below reported EBITDA ($15.2M), which is unusual for an adjusted measure. Our own draft lacks a standalone open-source (GPLv3) rep; the markup adds a generic one (4.10(f)); the playbook requires a schedule of 23 components and integration method.

6. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE
1) Escalate now (Westbrook, Hartwell; Thornton if fund-level). 2) Send Voss a short reply requiring a true redline and objecting to untracked changes and unrecorded "agreement." 3) Open with a package: hold Priority 1 items (escrow/setoff, cap >= 8.5%, tipping basket, knowledge/inquiry, Delaware law, 2-year nationwide non-compete, survival >= 15 months, Northland condition, parties/joint-and-several, uncapped fraud, exclusivity). 4) Use Priority 3 trades (3 to 2 year non-compete; 10% to 8.5% cap; 0.75% to 1.0% basket) and an offered 12-month 50% escrow release. 5) Fix HSR and set the outside date at 9/30. 6) Confirm 338 status before trading. 7) Obtain specific indemnities (IRS, Sept. 2023 incident, contractor IP) in Schedule 8.2.
